subject.note: sha256 over every audited HTML file and stylesheet, path-qualified. A human attestation against a criterion this scanner cannot decide is bound to this digest and stops being in force the moment it moves — a ruling about a page is not a ruling about its rewrite.

conformance.note: A criterion this scanner cannot decide statically blocks a conformance claim the same way a failure does. "unverified" means exactly that — not "probably fine".

findings.detail: <html> has no lang attribute — a screen reader cannot pick a voice
input with no label, aria-label or <label for>: <input type="text" name="q">

criteria.name: Meaningful Sequence
criteria.why: as above: reading order is judged, not parsed
criteria.howToVerify: Panel left. Turn CSS off entirely (DevTools ▸ disable the stylesheet, or Reader mode) and read top to bottom. The order content ARRIVES in must still make sense — a heading before the table it introduces, a coverage banner before the rows it qualifies. This panel is where that matters most: if a findings table arrives before the banner saying the scan was a VOID, the unstyled reading order tells a different story from the styled one.

criteria.name: Contrast (Minimum)
criteria.why: no stylesheet with custom properties was found to evaluate

criteria.name: Non-text Contrast
criteria.why: needs the rendered UI: which borders/icons are meaningful boundaries is a design judgement
criteria.howToVerify: Panel left, DevTools colour picker right. This is about NON-text: every control boundary and every icon that carries meaning needs 3:1 against what sits behind it. Check the input and select borders (--line / --line2 on --panel), the focus ring, the pill borders, and the status dot inside each pill. Do NOT re-check text here — 1.4.3 already machine-checks that. Judge only the shapes.

criteria.name: Focus Order
criteria.why: MEANINGFUL order cannot be read off the DOM — a sensible tab sequence is a human judgement
criteria.howToVerify: Panel left, hands off the mouse. Tab from the top and say the order aloud: skip link, identity row, tab strip, then content. It must match how the page reads visually AND make sense as a sequence. The three failures to hunt: a control that jumps backwards, a dialog that lets focus escape behind it, and anything Tab reaches that you cannot see.

criteria.name: Focus Not Obscured (Minimum)
criteria.why: needs a live browser: whether a sticky header covers the focused element is a rendered-layout fact
criteria.howToVerify: Panel on the left, nothing else needed. Click the first tab, then press Tab all the way down the page and watch the focus ring — it must stay FULLY visible at every stop. The failure to look for is the sticky identity bar covering a focused control when you Tab back upward, or a focused table row scrolling under it. Scroll to mid-page FIRST, then Tab: that is when it bites.

criteria.name: Target Size (Minimum)
criteria.why: needs a browser: 24x24 CSS px is a COMPUTED size, and this panel sizes controls in rem against a root font it adjusts at runtime
criteria.howToVerify: Panel left, DevTools right (Cmd-Opt-I). Inspect the small controls — the tab-strip buttons, the ⏺ re-scan buttons, the copy / hand-off buttons on remediation cards. Read width and height in the Computed pane: each needs 24x24 CSS px, OR 24px of clear spacing around it. The ⏺ buttons are the likeliest failure. Check at a NARROW window too — the root font scales with the viewport, so that is the small end.

criteria.name: Redundant Entry
criteria.why: needs flow analysis across a multi-step process; judgement, not markup
criteria.howToVerify: Panel left, a second tab of the same panel right. Walk one multi-step flow end to end: log in, then a remediation hand-off (pick a check, choose an engine, pick a model, submit). Nothing you already supplied may be asked for again unless it is re-entered deliberately for security. A step that re-requests what an earlier step already holds is the failure.
